li.p: The SaxonC 12 release is built from the Java source code of SaxonJ 12, with some variations.

SaxonC is now compiled to a native executable using GraalVM Native Image (version 22.3.0). (Earlier versions used Excelsior Jet, which is no longer marketed or supported.) GraalVM performs ahead-of-time compilation of the Java source code to executable machine code: the target code is specific to an operating system (Windows, Linux, or MacOS) and CPU architecture (AArch64 and Intel x86_64 for MacOS).
The move from Excelsior JET to GraalVM has a number of benefits:

ul.li: GraalVM is actively developed and supported by Oracle, and has excellent performance.

We can now deliver (for each target platform) a single shared native library which contains all the code required at run time, that is the application classes, standard library classes, the language runtime, and statically linked native code from the JDK.

li.p: All editions of SaxonC are currently built using GraalVM Community Edition.

SaxonC now uses the Native Image C API instead of JNI Invocation API for calling methods embedded in a native (that is, non-Java) shared library. There are benchmarks available which show that using the Native Image C API is considerably faster than using JNI.

The SaxonC Python extension is now available as a Python wheel package. This is available using PyPI for a number of platforms and flavors including MacOS, Linux and Windows. Python 3.8+ is supported.
SaxonC now works with PHP 8 and has removed support for PHP 7 since it is no longer supported.
In SaxonC 12.0, a few features from SaxonC 11.x have not yet been bridged to GraalVM, in particular:
Localization using ICU4J. (Localization using the capabilities of the JDK remains available, but is more limited.)
Calls to user-written host language extension functions.
We hope to restore these features (perhaps in a slightly different form) in the future.
Localization using ICU4J is now available.
The main Saxon 12 documentation has been updated to provide more details relevant for the C/C++, PHP and Python platforms where this differs to Saxon on the Java and C# platforms.
Updated to version 22.3.1 of GraalVM Native Image, used to compile SaxonC to a native executable.

ul.li: ICU localization is currently not supported.
Host language extension functions are currently not supported.
The new methods clarkNameToEQName() and EQNameToClarkName() are available on the SaxonProcessor class across the languages C++, PHP and Python.
The flag argument in the setCatalog() method of SaxonProcessor has been dropped.

A number of methods have been added to the Xslt30Processor class to better support exporting an XSLT stylesheet to SEF: setFastCompilation(), setRelocatable(), setTargetEdition() and setXsltLanguageVersion(). These methods are available across all languages (C++, PHP and Python).

Exceptions that are thrown from the underlying Java code are now handled in the C++ API and re-thrown as a C++ exception called SaxonApiException. Likewise these exceptions are thrown in the Python API as PySaxonApiError and in the PHP extension as PHP exceptions. Note: For the Python API on Windows the PySaxonApiError is not available therefore we throw RuntimeError if there are any failures.
The setStreaming() and isStreaming() methods have been added to XQueryProcessor.

The setLanguageVersion() method has been added to XPathProcessor and XQueryProcessor; this can be used to enable use of the experimental 4.0 extensions with SaxonC-PE and SaxonC-EE (as documented in the main Saxon 12 documentation).
The registerSchemaFromNode() method has been added to SchemaValidator.
PySaxonApiError is now supported on Windows as on other platforms (removing this restriction in SaxonC 12.1).
The set_language_version() method has belatedly been added to the Python PyXPathProcessor API.
The XPath 4.0 fn:parse-html() function is now supported.
The getXslMessages() method is added back into the C++, Python and PHP APIs on the XsltExecutable class.
Added the method PyXPathProcessor.set_base_uri() (see bug issue #6064).
Added the PyXdmNode.local_name property (see bug issue #6065).

Added the node axis feature to get the array of nodes reachable from the current node via a given axis. Axis options are as follows: ANCESTOR = 0, ANCESTOR_OR_SELF = 1, ATTRIBUTE = 2, CHILD = 3, DESCENDANT = 4, DESCENDANT_OR_SELF = 5, FOLLOWING = 6, FOLLOWING_SIBLING = 7, NAMESPACE = 8, PARENT = 9, PRECEDING = 10, PRECEDING_SIBLING = 11, SELF = 12. See the axisNodes() method on the XdmNode class (C++, PHP and Python).

The importPackage(const char * filename) method is added to the C++, Python and PHP APIs on the Xslt30Processor class. This method supports the xsl:use-package declaration to import a library package before compiling a primary stylesheet or package.

The PyXdmNode now implements the built-in function len() to return the number of children at a given node. Note this is different to the size() method inherited from PyXdmValue which gets the number of items in a sequence, and so returns the value 1 for a PyXdmNode.

The SaxonC Python API now supports the subscript operator (i.e. square brackets []) on PyXdmValue and PyXdmNode objects. For example, given a node object n and integer i, n[i] returns the i'th child node of n or None if the i'th child does not exist. Then n[i][j] returns the j'th child node of n[i], and so on. For a PyXdmValue object, n[i] returns the i'th item in the sequence.
Added ICU localization support for SaxonC-EE and SaxonC-PE.
The C API is now documented: see SaxonC C API.
The setcatalog() method on the SaxonProcessor class has been enhanced in the C++, Python and PHP APIs to accept multiple catalog files.
Added support for parsing JSON documents from file and string. This feature has been added to the SaxonProcessor as parseJsonFromFile() and parseJsonFromString() in the C++, Python and PHP APIs.
The method setUnprefixedElementMatchingPolicy() has been added to the XPathProcessor class in the C++, Python and PHP APIs.

Added the option to specify the encoding for parsing XML documents from strings (including when compiling a stylesheet from a string using the Xslt30Processor.compileFromString() method). If the encoding is not set then the platform default is used.

PHP API: added the methods XdmNode.getAttributeNodes() and XdmNode.getChildren() which respectively return the attribute nodes, and child nodes, of the current node, as a PHP array of XdmNode objects.
We have thoroughly reviewed how we handle paths passed in by the user so that they are now getting properly resolved with the 'current working directory'. (see bug issue #6273)
The build scripts for the command line programs for Linux, MacOS, and Windows have been updated and renamed. For details see "Command line interface" at Running SaxonC.
The methods getLineNumber() and getColumnNumber() have been added to the XdmNode class in the C++, Python and PHP APIs.
The clearXslMessages() method has been added to the XsltExecutable class in the C++, Python and PHP APIs.

The move to a different JVM technology inevitably changes the mechanisms for product installation and configuration. Please see the documentation for details: for instance Installing SaxonC, and the installation documentation for the PHP extension and Python extension.

The SAXONC_HOME environment variable is no longer used for the location of the installed SaxonC library. Dynamic linking of the library is done according to the system default. For example, for a unix system lookup is done according to the path /lib, and then /usr/lib (or /usr/local/lib for MacOS). In some systems the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable can be used instead.

For Python users, the product is now available as a Python wheel package on PyPI, for multiple platforms. This means that it can be installed with pip, which greatly simplifies the installation process. See Python extension for details.
For MacOS, SaxonC is now available for the AArch64 architecture as well as the Intel x86_86 architecture.

li.p: Some changes have been made to the structure of the SaxonC product downloads:

ul.li: The download directory has been restructured to move the core library file into the libs/[nix|darwin|win] directory.
The Windows download is now presented as a .zip file rather than an .exe file.
The python source code has been moved out of the Saxon.C.API/python-saxon directory to the top-level under the pypi directory.
From 12.3, GLIBC 2.32 is no longer a minimum prerequisite for SaxonC. SaxonC now now works on older versions of GLIBC, allowing users to run the product on these systems.
Compiling the C++ API now requires at least C++ 14. This also affects the building of the Python and PHP APIs.
ICU localization support added in SaxonC-PE and SaxonC-EE, to provide support for formatting numbers and dates, as well as sorting and comparison of strings, in a wide variety of languages.
Improved memory management for the handling of XDM objects.
Multi threading feature added to the Xslt30Processor and XQueryProcessor (see: bug issue #4428).
Better encoding of strings: redesigned the handling of string between the C++ JNI API and the internal Java API.

Replaced the getXslMessages() method from the XsltProcessor and Xslt30Processor with the new XsltExecutable method setSaveXslMessage(). This new method gives users the option to direct xsl:message output to the standard error listener (by default). Alternatively the xsl:message output can be sent to the given file name.

For XSLT transformations, the compilation and execution of a stylesheet is now separated as follows:
The Xslt30Processor is used to compile an XSLT stylesheet, returning an XsltExecutable representing the compiled form of the stylesheet. Methods on the XsltExecutable can then be used to invoke the transform. The new XsltExecutable class is added in the C++, Python, and PHP APIs.
The one shot methods transformFileToString(), transformFiletoValue() and transformFileToFile() are retained on Xslt30Processor for backwards compatibility, but the use of the corresponding methods on the XsltExecutable class is recommended.
It is possible to clone the XsltExecutable object to run different executables.
The XsltProcessor has now been dropped from the product given that the Xslt30Processor and XsltExecutable covers the same features.

XdmArray and XdmMap have been implemented as new XDM data types, making it easier to pass maps and arrays as parameters to queries or stylesheets. (These classes have been available in SaxonJ since version 9.8, and are belatedly added to the SaxonC API.) The superclass XdmFunctionItem is also implemented, and provides the methods call() and getSystemFunction() for working with XDM functions.
The SchemaValidator now supports exporting to schema component model (SCM) files. Users can now create a precompiled schema and export to a SCM file.

A new option enables the xsl:result-document output from an XSLT transform to be captured and saved in a map, where it is subsequently accessible using the URI as a key. This mechanism is available on the XsltExecutable class via the new setCaptureResultDocuments() and getResultDocument() methods.

SaxonC 11 introduces a change to the version numbering policy, to align with the numbering used for the corresponding SaxonJ (Java) product (where the change was introduced with Saxon 10), so the major version number jumps from 1.2 to 11. Three-part version numbers are now used: major releases will be numbered 11, 12, etc; maintenance releases will use the second component 11.1, 11.2 and so on; while the third digit will be used only to distinguish internal or limited-release builds. Download files will carry the two-part version number in their names, for example libsaxon-EEC-setup64-v11.1.zip.

The first release of SaxonC in the version 11 series is 11.1, built from SaxonJ 11.1 (which is released at the same time). This means that for the first time, the latest SaxonC release is also built from the latest SaxonJ release. In the future, the intention is that maintenance releases (11.2, 11.3, etc.) will be released on all platforms (Java, .NET, and C/C++, PHP, and Python) at the same time.

From Saxon 11, the versions of the products for the different platforms are now referred to as the following: SaxonJ is the Java product, SaxonCS is the C# product for .NET, and SaxonC is the product for C/C++, PHP, and Python. Note that SaxonC was previously known as Saxon/C. The different editions of the SaxonC product are now called SaxonC-HE, SaxonC-PE, and SaxonC-EE (rather than Saxon-HE/C, Saxon-PE/C, and Saxon-EE/C, as previously).
Updated the core XSLT processor to the Java Saxon 9.9.1.5 version.
Updated APIs: Support for XSLT 3.0, XQuery 3.1, XPath 3.1 and Schema Validation 1.0/1.1.

Added a feature rich XSLT 3.0 processor API to the languages: C++, PHP 7.2 and Python. Therefore two XSLT Processor classes are now available for each language supported:
C++ APIs: XsltProcessor and Xslt30Processor
Python APIs: PyXsltProcessor and PyXslt30Processor
PHP APIs: Saxon\XsltProcessor and Saxon\Xslt30Processor
Added Python3 API to the suite of programming languages supported by SaxonC. The Python extension was implemented using Cython.
Updated to Excelsior JET Enterprise 15.3 (MP1) cross compiler tool.
Additional methods in the APIs for XSLT and XQuery in C++ and PHP. (Also supported in the new Python API.)
XML Catalog file support in SaxonC.

SaxonC (all editions) can load stylesheets generated in the form of SEF files either by SaxonC itself, or by SaxonJ-EE 9.9. SaxonC-EE can also generate SEF files for use by SaxonJ, SaxonC, or SaxonJS.

The following bugs have been fixed:
Bug #2055: Apache allocates a lot of memory without releasing it
Bug #3837: Cannot locate the built PHP extension in Saxon/HE for Mac OS X
Bug #4274: Using a catalog file with Saxon in PHP
Bug #4302: High memory usage with SaxonC + PHP
Updated the core XSLT processor to the Java Saxon 9.8.0.4 version.
Updated APIs: Support for XSLT 3.0, XQuery 3.1, XPath 2.0/3.0 and Schema Validation 1.0/1.1.
Added XDM Data Model API in support of the specs XPath, XQuery, XSLT and Schema Validation.
Support for user defined functions. Users can now write their functions in C++/PHP and invoke them in XSLT, XQuery and XPath.
Support for PHP7 distribution.
Windows SaxonC builds.
Updated to Excelsior JET 11.3 (MP1) cross compiler tool.
Revised API for XSLT and XQuery in C, C++ and PHP.
